Fix movement-floor DST bug and coach API-key reuse across endpoint changes (#375)

* Fix movement-floor DST bug and coach API-key reuse across endpoint changes

Two independent issues surfaced while reviewing PR #374, neither caused
by that PR but found in the same pass:

- movement_floor_policy.dart: daysSinceFrozen computed the gap with
  to.difference(from).inDays on local-time DateTimes. A span crossing
  a spring-forward transition loses an hour of wall-clock duration, so
  a real 10-day gap (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-11) floored to 9. Fixed by
  diffing UTC-normalized calendar dates instead, matching the pattern
  dayLabelBefore already documents and follows for the same reason.

- coach.dart setup screen: the API key field was seeded once from
  CoachConfig and never revisited, while switching presets or editing
  the base URL changed only the endpoint. Saving then sent the old
  key to whatever origin was currently in the field — a stale cloud
  key could reach a newly-selected local/private endpoint, or vice
  versa, without the user re-entering or confirming it (CWE-200,
  flagged by CodeRabbit as Major). Added coachEndpointOrigin() in
  coach_config.dart and used it to track which origin the key field's
  contents belong to; the key is now cleared (and deleted from the
  keychain on save) whenever the base URL's origin actually changes.

Adds test/coach_endpoint_origin_test.dart; movement_floor_policy_test.dart
already encoded the correct expected values and needed no changes.

* Fix key-clear message loss and unreadable-key leak across endpoint changes

Two issues flagged on PR #375 against the origin-change key-clearing fix:

- Tapping a preset set _base.text (firing _onBaseChanged synchronously,
  which sets _msg to explain a cleared key) and then unconditionally
  reset _msg to null in the same setState, silently discarding that
  explanation. _msg is now cleared BEFORE _base.text is assigned.

- A key that exists but could not be read (CoachConfig.keyUnreadable)
  seeds the setup screen's key field empty, indistinguishable from "no
  key was ever set." _pendingKeyDelete was only ever armed when the
  field was visibly non-empty, so this case bypassed it: the stale,
  unreadable key survived an endpoint change untouched and could later
  be sent to the new endpoint (CWE-522, Major). _pendingKeyDelete is
  now armed on every endpoint change regardless of the field's visible
  contents, and the whole decision is extracted into a pure function,
  coachApiKeyToSave(), so the interaction is unit-testable without a
  widget tree.

Adds test/coach_api_key_to_save_test.dart covering all four
(readable/unreadable stored key) x (pending/not-pending) combinations
with an empty field, plus the non-empty-field case.

* whitespace-only key input bypassed pending key deletion

 don't treat whitespace-only key input as a real replacement.

CodeRabbit flagged this on PR #375 (CWE-200, Major) after the previous
fix landed: the _key controller's listener cleared _pendingKeyDelete
on raw `_key.text.isNotEmpty`, but coachApiKeyToSave trims the field
before deciding what to save. Whitespace-only input (e.g. a stray
pasted space) is non-empty by the raw check, so it cancelled the
pending deletion — then Save saw an effectively empty, non-pending
field and, for an unreadable stored key, left it untouched in the
keychain instead of deleting it. Same leak class the endpoint-change
fix was meant to close, just reachable through whitespace.

Extracted the decision into coachKeyFieldHasReplacement() in
coach_config.dart (trims before checking, so it can't drift from
coachApiKeyToSave's own trimming) and used it in place of the inline
check.

Adds test/coach_key_field_has_replacement_test.dart.

* stop tracking "replacement typed" as mutable state, derive it at Save

CodeRabbit found a gap in the EDGE-13 fix on PR #375: the _key listener
cleared _pendingKeyDelete as soon as any non-whitespace text appeared,
but never restored it. Typing a replacement key after an endpoint
change and then erasing it again left the flag cleared with nothing to
show for it — an unreadable stored key from the old endpoint then
survived _save() untouched and could reach the new endpoint on a later
load (CWE-200).

Rather than patch the listener again, removed it. coachApiKeyToSave
already derives "is there a real replacement" correctly by checking
_key.text.trim() at the moment Save actually runs, so tracking it
separately as mutable state was both redundant and the source of two
bugs in a row (this one and EDGE-13's whitespace case). _pendingKeyDelete
now only ever means "the endpoint changed since the stored key was
last confirmed to belong to it" — set by _onBaseChanged, cleared after
a successful save, untouched by typing.

Removes the now-unused coachKeyFieldHasReplacement() and its test.
Adds a regression case to coach_api_key_to_save_test.dart: a
replacement typed after an endpoint change and then erased (to blank
or whitespace) is still force-deleted at Save time.

* bump kAlgoVersion for daysSinceFrozen DST fix

fix: atomic db-backed slot allocation for notification ids (#415)

* fix: atomic db-backed slot allocation for notification ids

_slotFor was doing a plain read-then-write over shared_preferences with
no lock or transaction, so two isolates (foreground app + headless
BLE/BGTask sync) allocating for two different dedupeKeys in the same
category at the same time could both land on the same slot -> same OS
notification id -> one show() call silently replaces the other. same
bug class fired_keys.dart already fixed for the fire-once guard via an
atomic sqlite INSERT OR IGNORE, so give slot allocation the same
treatment: new notif_slots table + UNIQUE(category, slot) index,
claimNotifSlot does one atomic get-or-insert. shared_preferences kept
as a mirror + degraded-mode fallback when there's no db.

schema 53. no kAlgoVersion bump, this is notification plumbing not
analytics output.

* address review: bound probe loop, guard bandSize, log DB-fallback degrade, fix test claim

- cap maxProbes to bandSize (a stale hint could otherwise re-probe already-claimed slots up to 1024 times for no gain)
- guard bandSize <= 0 and normalize startAt % bandSize before probing
- log (not silently swallow) when the DB slot claim fails and we degrade to the SharedPreferences fallback, since that reopens the race this PR closes
- reworded notification_ids_atomic_test.dart's header/test comment: Future.wait doesn't force true SQLite-level interleaving in one isolate (the write lock serializes it), so it proves the UNIQUE-index claim is collision-free rather than reproducing the actual cross-isolate race

* fix: db-backed slot must win over a diverged prefs mirror on every read

_slotFor checked the SharedPreferences mirror BEFORE ever trying the DB
claim, so a stale/diverged prefs entry (partial write, pre-migration
leftover) would win over the DB forever after the first allocation --
the DB was only ever authoritative on first write, not on read. move
the DB claim ahead of the prefs check so it runs on every call; the
prefs existing-slot check now only applies inside the degraded
fallback (no DB in this process).

added a regression test that corrupts the prefs mirror to point at a
different slot than the DB owns and asserts the DB value wins.

fix: serialize widget push() so concurrent calls can't interleave (#416)

resume, post-derive, and bg-wake all fire WidgetService.refresh->push()
unawaited with no lock. push() writes ~20 keys with an await between
each, so two overlapping calls could interleave their writes and land
a snapshot mixing fields from two different days. chain push() through
a static future so overlapping calls run strictly one after another.

coach: close recursive-CTE DoS in the SQL guard (#419)

* coach: close recursive-CTE DoS in the SQL guard

a recursive CTE's working table is an ephemeral btree, which layer 2
(_assertAllowedBtrees) deliberately ignores since it only tracks
OpenRead/OpenWrite/ReopenIdx. that meant `WITH RECURSIVE x(n) AS (...)
SELECT count(*) FROM x` touched zero real views/tables and sailed
through both guard layers, then ran unbounded on the read-only handle
with no progress handler or timeout anywhere in the call chain.

ban RECURSIVE at the keyword layer (the coach has no legit use for one
over 7 small derived views), and add a 10s timeout + handle-reset
backstop in runCoachSql for the sibling case the guard can't structurally
catch (a big cross-join of allowed views) so a slow query wedges the next
turn instead of leaving the coach permanently stuck.

* coach: address review — valid-SQL adversarial case, close() teardown guard

- the multi-CTE adversarial case used syntax SQLite doesn't accept
  (RECURSIVE mid-list); replaced with the real form (RECURSIVE right
  after WITH, applying to all CTEs in the statement) so it actually
  exercises what it claims to.
- added a test documenting the deliberate trade-off that 'recursive'
  is now unusable as a CTE/alias name too (blanket keyword ban, not
  position-sensitive) — the coach never needs that name.
- wrap the close() on timeout in try/catch so a teardown failure can't
  swallow the timeout error response.

cycleDay/cycleGaps/byCycleDay/predicted next-period all used raw

fix: local BYOK endpoints were sending literal "Bearer null" (#438)

postChat always built the Authorization header from config.apiKey, but
a local endpoint (Ollama/LM Studio) is allowed to be configured with no
key at all. null interpolates straight into the header string, so every
request to a keyless local endpoint went out as "Bearer null" - a proxy
that actually checks the header rejects it with a 401 that just shows
up as an opaque provider error.

omit the header entirely when there's no key, same as any other
OpenAI-compatible client would.

fix route tracker dropping gps tail when stop() races an in-flight flush (#439)

stop() only ever awaited its own two _flush() calls, never an
auto-triggered flush from _onSample. if that auto-flush's sink call
failed after stop() had already run its own flushes and disposed, the
requeued batch sat in _buffer forever with nothing left to flush it -
silent tail data loss.

serialize flushes through one chained future and have stop() await it
before doing its own flush, so a late requeue is caught instead of
orphaned.

fix: await live activity end before starting a new one (#440)

start() fired act.end() in an unawaited Task then immediately called
Activity.request() right after — nothing sequenced the two, so ending
a workout and starting one again fast (or backgrounding right after
start) could leave a stale activity alongside the new one on lock
screen / dynamic island. made start/update/end async and await the
ActivityKit calls directly instead of spawning detached tasks, and
route the method channel through Task { await ...; result(nil) } so
the channel result only fires once the real work is done. same fix in
both the workout and breathing bridges.

docs: iOS background band-prompt design and implementation plan

sync: BandPromptPolicy and suspension-aware liveness policies

Pure decisions for the iOS background change: who programs the band's
HIGH_FREQ_SYNC prompt (smart wake beats the 15-min background keep-alive,
a background lease renews past half-way), a keep-alive fuse that ignores
silence accumulated while the process could not run, and a resume verdict
that probes a quiet no-stream link instead of tearing it down.

ble: suspension-aware keep-alive fuse and probeLink()

A tick that arrives more than two periods late means the process was
suspended (iOS between band prompts); the fuse restarts its clock there
and the forced battery poll does the asking. probeLink() sends
GET_BATTERY_LEVEL and reports whether a reply correlated, for resume paths
that must not guess. Exposes highFreqReason/highFreqUntil for the caller
that programs the prompt.

ios: wake on band prompts instead of holding a 1 Hz HR stream in background

The iosBackgroundKeepalive owner held the realtime-HR stream the whole
time the app was backgrounded, purely so the inbound 1 Hz notification
kept the suspended process schedulable: ~86,400 wakes a day, 62% of a
day's battery with 20 min on screen. Background now owns nothing on
either platform; instead the band is asked to prompt us every 15 min via
ENTER_HIGH_FREQ_SYNC (2 h lease, renewed from the existing 25-min
background tick), and the engine's existing prompt handler runs the
offload. Foreground resume and the BG-task catch-up probe a quiet link
before reusing it rather than reconnecting on every open.

ios: arm the band prompt on the background cold-launch path too

A restore relaunch after a process kill lands in _init's background
branch, not openSession. It reconciled live streams (now: none on iOS)
but never programmed the prompt, so a relaunched process had no wake
source until a foreground open. Review finding on #445.

review: clear prompt state on every teardown, serialize prompt refreshes, sync spec

- _teardownSession clears _highFreqReason/_highFreqUntil/_highFreqModeRequested
  on unintentional drops too, not only in the next connect's setup.
- _refreshHighFreqWakeWindow is single-flight and coalescing (same shape as
  the engine's live reconciler) so a stale background pass can never outlive
  a newer foreground pass and leave the band prompting with the engine
  believing it asked for it.
- Spec's BandPromptPolicy contract now matches the implementation.

ble: pin HIGH_FREQ_SYNC enter/exit writes to their session

Capture the session and link generation before each write, pass the
session as the write owner, and only mutate the high-frequency state if
that link is still the live one — a continuation resuming after a
reconnect must neither claim the mode on a successor that never got the
ENTER nor clear what the successor has since programmed. Review finding
on #445.

fix: BLE notify hot-path exceptions, cycle_screen mounted guards, O(n^2) baseline scan

ble_engine.dart: wrap the notify-callback body and _onFrame in try/catch —
neither had one, the one gap in a file that otherwise contains every
failure path. A malformed chunk on an unusual firmware revision was an
uncaught async error that silently killed that characteristic's whole
notification stream instead of degrading (log + drop that chunk/frame).

cycle_screen.dart: _setEnabled/_logStart called context.read<AppState>()
after an unguarded await, the one outlier in a file where every sibling
handler already guards with `if (!mounted) return;` first. Also swapped
the whole-object context.watch<AppState>() backing _lengthReview for a
narrow context.select — that subtree was rebuilding on all 87
notifyListeners() call sites (including live HR/sync ticks) to read one
profile bool.

derivation_engine.dart: maxBefore/valuesBefore full-rescanned the whole
frozen baseline series on every call, once per baseline key per target
day during a sweep — O(n^2) over days of history on a version-bump
recompute. Added a prefix-max array + binary search (the series is
already date-ascending and frozen for the sweep) to make both O(log n).

coach_engine.dart: _deriveTitle's null-check narrowed a separately
`??`-defaulted expression rather than `it.text` itself — correct only
because both read the same field the same way; rewritten to narrow once.

fix: isolate onOffloadState callback failure, null-safe prefix-max lookup

Two real findings from the PR's own bot review, verified:

- _setOffloadActive calls the caller-supplied onOffloadState hook
  synchronously from _enqueueOffloadFrame, BEFORE it kicks off
  _drainOffloadFrames. An exception there (a buggy UI callback) would
  propagate out and skip starting the drain for that frame — the frame
  was already queued, so it self-heals on the next enqueue, but there's
  no reason to depend on that. Isolated in its own try/catch so a
  callback failure can never block the queue/drain state machine.
- maxBefore's _prefixMax[key]! is unreachable today (every key in
  _series has a matching _prefixMax entry built in the same
  constructor), confirmed by both the bot and by reading the
  constructor — but ?[...] costs nothing and survives a future
  refactor that builds one map without the other.

The other two bot suggestions (resetting offload latches on a chunk-
parse failure, and a speculative _lengthReview-outside-build path) were
checked and are not real: the first would reset unrelated offload state
on an unrelated framing error, and the second call site (_lengthReview)
is only ever invoked from build() today. Left as-is.

fix evening briefing fallback and stale row after writing one

Two issues flagged on PR #447:

- currentBriefingPeriod documents that past 17:00 it returns `evening`
  even before the evening recap exists, "falling back to the cached
  morning one until [it] exists" — but the briefing row just opened
  whatever period that function returned, so after 5pm with nothing
  written yet it showed the generic empty prompt and opened a bare
  evening screen instead of the morning briefing already in cache
  (Sourcery). Extracted the fallback into a pure function,
  resolveBriefingToShow(), in ai/briefing.dart.

- BriefingStore.write (called from BriefingEngine.generate) never
  bumps AppState.insightsRevision, so RevisionReload's automatic
  reload never fires for it. The row read BriefingStore synchronously
  at build time with no way to know a briefing was written during the
  visit, so returning from AiBriefingScreen after writing one left
  Home showing the stale/empty subtitle until an unrelated revision
  bump happened to refresh it (CodeRabbit). The row now pushes the
  route directly (go() discards the pushed route's Future), awaits
  it, and calls reload() if still mounted.

Adds test/resolve_briefing_to_show_test.dart (4 cases: morning as-is,
evening with its own recap, evening falling back to morning, evening
with neither written yet).

Fix stale briefing period captured by Home's IndexedStack-kept-alive tap closure

CodeRabbit found a staleness gap on PR #447: the briefing door's
onTap closure captured `foundPeriod` (and the cached briefing used
for the subtitle) from whatever build last ran. Home is kept alive
indefinitely by the shell's IndexedStack (app_shell.dart), so a build
can sit for hours without rerunning. Long enough to span the 17:00
morning/evening boundary, or to miss a briefing written in the
background after that build. Tapping the row in that window could
navigate to the wrong period.

Extracted the period+cache resolution into _resolveBriefingNow(),
called once at build time for the subtitle and again fresh inside the
onTap closure right before constructing AiBriefingScreen, so a tap
always reflects the actual current time and the latest stored
briefing rather than whatever was true when Home last rebuilt.
